plan: This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy, regardless of other bidders' behavior. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down. Bidding exactly my value of $22 ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value exceeds the second-highest bid) and never overpay. This is the theoretically optimal strategy in this auction format.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid regardless of my own bid, so bidding above my value risks losses, and bidding below reduces my chance of winning profitable auctions. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, and standard auction theory confirming truthful bidding is optimal, I will bid exactly my value of $15.

This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. If I bid higher than my value, I risk winning at a price above my value and losing money. If I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. With my value at $10, I should bid exactly $10.
